### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/connector-app-stripe`, `@objectstack/connector-openapi`, touching **32** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/apps/connector-stripe/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via deepObject (literal, a string literal in query; a string literal in serializeQueryParameter))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/apps/connector-stripe/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **212** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **2** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 37184244b82b9e4234581b653cdc7554e74e6136` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f63a5da1c63f8fa68818014a1ce4598b201adea3` — the merge of head `73e2a2ec62142c8ad97cbec4619beb9ff9adc241` into base `37184244b82b9e4234581b653cdc7554e74e6136`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f63a5da1c63f8fa68818014a1ce4598b201adea3 && git checkout f63a5da1c63f8fa68818014a1ce4598b201adea3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 37184244b82b9e4234581b653cdc7554e74e6136 73e2a2ec62142c8ad97cbec4619beb9ff9adc241 && git checkout -B drift-repro 37184244b82b9e4234581b653cdc7554e74e6136 && git merge --no-ff 73e2a2ec62142c8ad97cbec4619beb9ff9adc241

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 37184244b82b9e4234581b653cdc7554e74e6136
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 37184244b82b9e4234581b653cdc7554e74e6136` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**ACCEPT** at head `73e2a2ec` · `Implemented-by:` `claude/issue-28504-openapi-param-style` · `Reviewed-by:` this seat (lane ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`). `Clause-②: no`. No `packages/spec` file is touched, so no `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record is owed.

| Check | Result |
|:--|:--|
| Shape | Draft, base `main`. First line is `Fixes #28504`, the only closing keyword. |
| Scope | 6 files, +696/−29. Not governed (0 of 6 paths hit the register). One `@objectstack/connector-openapi` patch changeset. |
| Ruling | Triage 6553109544 is followed. Every path, query and header value is encoded by its declared `style` / `explode`, or by the OAS 3.x default for its location. A style that OAS 3.x does not define for the location refuses the operation at materialization, naming the operation and the parameter; an `include` that leaves the operation out clears the refusal. A value the style cannot carry fails the dispatch before any fetch. No non-scalar value reaches `String()`. |
| Evidence | 17 cases, including the three Stripe shapes with GetInvoices' five parameter objects copied verbatim; their canonical JSON equals the packaged `stripe.openapi.json`. The ablation turns 15 red and leaves exactly the 2 scalar controls green, which confirms scalars are byte-identical to before. A public-door probe through `POST /automation/:flow/trigger` sent `created%5Bgte%5D=…&due_date%5Bgte%5D=…&expand%5B0%5D=data.customer&expand%5B1%5D=data.subscription`. Stripe's own answer is NOT MEASURED (no key). |
| Gates | Local: 88 derived, 88 run, 0 unrun. CI on the head is still running: 14 success, 12 skipped, 21 in progress, none red so far. |
| Accepted deviation | `packages/apps/connector-stripe/README.md` is outside the claimed surface. Its Limits bullet told authors to leave `expand` / `created` out, and this change makes that false. Correcting it in the same PR is right. |
| Open question (dev: A, shipped) | `deepObject` on an array is undefined in OAS 3.x. Stripe declares it on `expand`. The seat keeps A (`expand[0]=a`), because it follows from the declared style's own rule and is also the indexed form Stripe's form decoder reads. Whether Stripe accepts it is NOT MEASURED. If a measurement with a key ever disagrees, a new card corrects it. |

**Noted, not filed (agreed):** cookie parameters are never sent, and `allowReserved` is not read. Both predate this PR, and neither has a public-door reach measured.

**Landing:** not governed. The seat lands it (`pr_ready` + `automerge_enable`) once CI on this head is green.
